title: Piano Movers in Santa Ana | SOS Moving
metaDescription: Piano movers in Santa Ana: four movers, blankets, straps and a padded board on one hourly job, with permit-district curbs and porch steps planned first.
heroSubtitle: A crew of four, blankets and straps for the instrument, and the rest of the home loaded on the same hourly clock.

faq.question: Do you charge a separate price to move a piano in Santa Ana?
faq.answer: No. The instrument rides on the hourly rate of the crew that carries it, with a flat $200 added for the piece itself. A crew of four is required, the job is billed for at least three hours, and an address 30 or more miles from our base starts at four hours instead.

faq.question: Can one visit cover the instrument and the rest of the house?
faq.answer: Yes, and that is how most of these jobs run. The same four movers load the bedrooms, the kitchen and the instrument on one clock, so there is no second crew to schedule and no second trip to pay for. Just tell us at booking that an instrument is on the list.

faq.question: Where does the truck end up parking on my block?
faq.answer: As close to the door as the code allows. The city limits a commercial vehicle of 10,000 pounds GVWR or more to two hours on a residential street, with an exception while it is loading or delivering, and some blocks also post a height restriction within 100 feet of the intersection. Our driver reads those signs before setting up.

faq.question: My condo has a garage underneath it. What should I arrange first?
faq.answer: Reserve the elevator and check the garage clearance against a moving truck. A building like Legado at the Met stacks 278 units over a four-level garage with three levels below ground, so the truck normally works from street level and the carry starts there. Should the association want a certificate of insurance on file, ours costs $50.

faq.question: Do you tune, appraise or store the instrument?
faq.answer: No. We move it and set it down where you want it standing, and that is where our part ends. Tuning and valuation belong to a technician once the instrument has settled into the new room.

faq.question: Can a crew come the same day I call?
faq.answer: Often yes. The line at 909-443-0004 is answered Monday through Sunday, 8AM to 6PM, and when a crew of four is free we can take the job that day. Dates that need a guest parking permit or a reserved elevator are better booked ahead.
